verdict_text: NO. The plan omits `h.<i>.attn.c_proj.weight` from its cast pattern, so only 36 matrices become bfloat16 instead of the 48 required by clause 1 of "Required result" — the 12 attention output projections stay float32. It compounds this by encoding the wrong number into the required checks (`count ... is: 36` and the dtype assertions built on the same 3-pattern regex), so the run will pass silently instead of failing loudly as the "Required checks" section demands ("exactly 48 tensors are bfloat16"). The remaining aspects (buffer deletion, name preservation, 148-tensor count, 64 MiB sharding with index) are handled correctly, but grading compares dtypes against the reference and will fail on those 12 tensors.
